global environment forever - update-environment refreshes SSH_CONNECTION

content.text:
Nothing in your dotfiles is at fault — no mode is set anywhere, and sway takes the connector's preferred mode. The problem is the DisplayPort link itself.

## What I found

Your monitor and GPU both advertise 4K@60 correctly:

- EDID preferred timing: **3840x2160 @ 60.00Hz, 533.25 MHz pixel clock**, interface = DisplayPort, 10 bpc, HDR
- Kernel lists `3840x2160` first in `/sys/class/drm/card1-DP-1/modes`
- `link-status = 0` (Good) — training succeeded, no error flagged

But when I asked sway for it, it reported `success` and silently stayed at 1440p. 4K@30 applied instantly. That gap is the tell:

| Mode | Payload @8bpc | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2560x1440@60 | 5.80 Gbps | works |
| 3840x2160@30 | 7.13 Gbps | works |

Your setting was working the whole time. The problem is different.

**What's actually happening:** the trailer is inside the heredoc Claude typed itself —

```
git add -A src tests && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
...
Claude-Session: ht...
```

Not appended by the attribution machinery. Proof it's working: if `attribution.sessionUrl` were being ignored, those commits would carry *two* trailers — the auto one plus the typed one. They carry one.

**Why it types it:** Claude reads `git log` before committing to match the repo's style. dissona has 6 commits with that trailer, zensourcer 57, handshake 36 — all written back when the auto-trailer was on. So it copies what looks like your convention. A mimicry loop the old setting seeded and the new setting can't break.

**Fix**, at `home-manager/claude-code/default.nix:60` — a global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (you had none), which loads into every session in every repo:

```nix
home.file.".claude/CLAUDE.md".text = ''
  ## Git commits

  Never put a `Claude-Session:` trailer, a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` line, or
  any other Claude or session attribution in a commit message or PR body -
  not even when existing commits in the repository have one. ...
'';
```

`lucie` evaluates. Apply with `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#lucie`.

Two caveats:

- **Existing commits keep their trailers** — this only affects new ones. The mimicry pressure fades as clean commits accumulate, which is why the instruction is explicit about ignoring what's already in history.
- **Restarting isn't enough for already-running sessions.** You have four Claude processes up, two running 3-4 days. `CLAUDE.md` is read at session start, so the long-lived ones won't pick it up until they're restarted.

I kept `attribution.sessionUrl = false` — it's doing its job on the automatic path. There's also an env-var escape hatch (`CLAUDE_CODE_SUPPRESS_SESSION_ATTRIBUTION`, checked before the setting) but it'd be redundant.
